question: Should OpenClaw core accept `{ owner }` records as a supported persisted `plugins.slots.*` config shape before write-side canonicalization and overwrite-invariant work lands?
rationale: The PR changes a public plugin/config contract and affects provider trust, startup, doctor, update, uninstall, memory, and context-engine paths; code repair alone cannot decide whether this is the desired permanent API direction.

options.title: Sponsor after repair
options.body: Accept the `{ owner }` direction only after the branch fixes the current blockers, rebases cleanly, and adds exact-head upgrade/runtime proof.

options.title: Pause behind role-slot work
options.body: Keep this PR open but require the owner-record shape to be folded into the broader multi-slot memory architecture before merge.

options.title: Decline core config widening
options.body: Close or ask for a new proposal if maintainers do not want object-form slot values in core config.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair
recommendation.body: Accept the `{ owner }` direction only after the branch fixes the current blockers, rebases cleanly, and adds exact-head upgrade/runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent slot-selection and plugin activation work makes this the best available routing candidate for the config/slot contract decision.
